$comment: Every pin, workaround and upstream-behaviour dependency this repository carries, in a form a scheduled check can poll: for each entry with an `upstream.api`, GET it and compare `state` (and, for crates, `max_stable_version`) against `state_when_recorded`. When it moves, do what `recheck` says. Recorded 2026-09-23.

entries.what: tauri-specta = "=2.0.0-rc.25" (Cargo.toml), with specta = "=2.0.0-rc.25" and, for tests/bindings.rs, specta-typescript = "=0.0.12".
entries.why: The house plugin standard requires tauri-specta for end-to-end types. It has never had a stable 2.0 release; its own crate docs tell users to pin with `=` during the rc period because the generated bindings change shape between rcs. The owner accepts the rc deliberately.
entries.waiting_on: A stable tauri-specta 2.0.0 (and the matching stable specta 2.0.0).
entries.recheck: When max_stable_version is non-null: move all three pins to the stable versions, run `UPDATE_BINDINGS=1 cargo test --test bindings`, review the diff of guest-js/bindings.ts, and update the README's tauri-specta section.

entries.what: Stock Tauri crashes in TauriActivity.onCreate on Android 7.x (API 24/25) with NoClassDefFoundError: java.lang.BootstrapMethodError, from jackson-databind 2.15.3's static initialiser — before any plugin, this guard included, is constructed. Measured on tauri 2.11.6 on the spike_api24_webview emulator: docs/verification/logs/cr53-stock-tauri-crash.logcat.txt.
entries.workaround: examples/tauri-app/android-7-jackson-workaround.zsh forces jackson-databind 2.12.7.1 and enables core library desugaring in the example's generated Gradle project, as reported working in the issue. The plugin itself does NOT impose this on consumers; the README tells apps to either raise minSdk to 26 or apply it themselves.
entries.waiting_on: Tauri downgrading or dropping jackson-databind in tauri-android (crates/tauri/mobile/android/build.gradle.kts), or declaring API 26 its real minimum.
entries.recheck: When the issue closes: check the jackson-databind version in the tauri crate's mobile/android/build.gradle.kts for the new Tauri release; run the example WITHOUT the workaround on an API 24 image; if it starts, delete the workaround script and the README paragraph.

entries.what: Tauri's injected IPC script uses object spread (`...options`, scripts/ipc-protocol.js line 77 in tauri 2.11.6), a Chromium 60 feature. On Chromium 53 it fails to parse, so window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.postMessage is never defined and every invoke() rejects with `TypeError: window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.postMessage is not a function`. Measured: docs/verification/screenshots/cr53-diag.png.
entries.why_it_matters_here: It is the premise for the dialog being native: an HTML fallback whose button calls invoke() is dead on exactly the engines it is for. The native dialog has no dependency on the IPC.

state_when_recorded.note: Raised in a 2026-07-17 comment on the same issue, not as its own issue.

entries.waiting_on: Nothing — this plugin does not depend on it being fixed.
entries.recheck: Informational. If Tauri ever ships an ES5 IPC script, the native dialog stays: it is strictly more robust.

entries.what: wry's Android loadUrlMainThread posts the app's first loadUrl to the main looper (wry 0.55.1 src/android/kotlin/RustWebView.kt), so it runs AFTER the plugin's load(webView) hook. Blanking the WebView inside load() alone is overtaken by that posted load — measured in the first version of this plugin.
entries.waiting_on: Nothing. The plugin blocks through Tauri's on_navigation hook, and re-neutralizes behind the posted load.
entries.recheck: On a wry bump: re-run docs/verification on the Chromium 109 arm and confirm the log still shows `refused navigation to http://tauri.localhost/` and no `page load started: http://tauri.localhost/`.

entries.what: `tauri ios init` writes project.yml only if it does not exist (tauri-v2.11.6 crates/tauri-cli/src/mobile/ios/project.rs, the `if !path.exists()` in the template generator), so changing bundle.iOS.minimumSystemVersion after the first init never reaches IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET. bundle.iOS.template is rendered with File::create on every init and does. The template path is resolved against the CLI's working directory, not src-tauri/. Tauri 2.11.6's default is 14.0 (tauri-utils ios_minimum_system_version); the dev branch says 15.0. All three measured: docs/verification/logs/ios-trap/.
entries.recheck: On a Tauri bump: re-copy crates/tauri-cli/templates/mobile/ios/project.yml at the new tag into examples/tauri-app/src-tauri/ios-project.yml, and re-run the three-step ios-trap check.
